summary: Towers are not the best fit for Floruvi. Land is not the limit, so the tower density advantage is worth little, while its costs are real: heads about 31% lighter (Touliatos 2016), one pump per tower, roots that dry in 30-60 minutes, and more labour per plant. If towers are used, 10 towers per 1,000 L sump is the best balance. It needs about 105 W (10.5 W per tower against 20 W) and 5.1-7.6 kWh per tower per month (against 14.4), costs about Rs 2,970 per tower plus about Rs 1,150 per tower for a shared inverter, and saves about Rs 25,000-34,000 per month at 600 towers. 20-tower clusters cost less per tower but do not cut power further with AC pumps, and one failure puts 1,800 plants at risk. The better system is aerated DWC float-support raft beds: about Rs 50 per site, 140 g base heads, 12-72 h of power-cut tolerance (estimate), and about Rs 19 per sellable kg core cost (capex over 5 years + power + labour). The same core cost is about Rs 37/kg for NFT, about Rs 47/kg for owner-made towers in clusters and about Rs 78/kg for bought tower kits. All-in with seeds, nutrients, polyhouse and RO water, the costs are about Rs 54, 77, 96 and 126 per kg. Build in phases tied to orders; 400 kg/week needs about 17,400 DWC sites (~725 m2).

risks: Disease spread: any shared reservoir (tower cluster or DWC bed) can move Pythium between plants. Australian growers lost 20-30% and sometimes whole summer crops; hot nutrient solution was the main factor, and moisture stress from stopped or pulsed flow also raised disease (Tesoriero, VG04012). Limit plants per reservoir, plant each reservoir all-in/all-out, sanitise between crops, keep solution at or below 25-26 C, and start with clean seedlings.

Centralising: the same report warns that one central tank raises the risk of losses from breakdowns and disease. This is why the recommendation is 10 towers per sump, not 20, and one solution per DWC bed.

Power cuts: towers and NFT roots dry within 30-60 minutes in hot weather. Any tower or NFT layout needs backup power and alarms. DWC needs only air-pump backup and tolerates hours without power (estimate).

Pump heat: a submersible pump puts all its power into the water. 20 W in a 30 L tank is 0.67 W/L (up to ~14 C per day of heat input before losses); 105 W in 1,000 L is 0.105 W/L. Small tanks run warmer (calculation).
Pump quality: aquarium and pond pumps (SOBO, Jebao) are not rated for farm duty. Keep one spare per 5-10 pumps and replace impellers yearly (estimate).

UV limits: UV units cost about Rs 13,000 each and add about 34 kWh per cluster per month (estimate). One study found that UV cut Pythium in the solution but did not reduce root rot. UV also breaks down iron chelates, so use a UV-stable chelate if UV is added (Arcas et al. 2025).
Hydrogen peroxide: in mineral nutrient solution, 37.5-75 mg/L stunted or killed lettuce. Use it only to clean empty tanks and lines between crops.

Water: RO is mandatory. Kratky and DWC concentrate salts when water is topped up. The first DWC fill needs about 250 L of RO water per m2 of bed, e.g. ~120 m3 for 400 kg/week. Check RO plant capacity and fill beds in phases. Decide solution replacement from lab tests, not a fixed monthly dump.
Mosquitoes breed in still DWC and Kratky water. Use insect screens and Bti (Kratky 2009).

Evidence gaps: all labour hours except the vertical-system proxy are estimates. Head weights in a Bengaluru polyhouse have not been measured. Pump flows use approximate curves. Indian DC-pump prices were not found. Cost per kg ranges are wide.
Demand: 600 towers (54,000 sites) would give about 800 kg/week at 90 g heads, twice the 400 kg/week a new seller sells by month 12. Capacity built ahead of buyers raises cost per sold kg.
recommendations: Main recommendation: build new capacity as aerated DWC float-support raft beds. Use 1.2 m wide, 25-30 cm deep beds, one solution per bed, one 100 W air pump per ~70 m2 plus a spare, and an inverter for the air pumps. Grow lettuce, arugula, pak choi, basil and kale. Estimated core cost is about Rs 19/kg, against about Rs 47/kg for owner-made towers in clusters and about Rs 78/kg for bought tower kits.

Pilot before scaling: build 4-6 beds (about 2,000 sites) next to one 10-tower cluster and run them for 2-3 cycles. Record sellable head weight, labour minutes, kWh, water, losses and solution temperature. Scale only in step with signed orders.

If towers are kept or already bought, run them as 10-tower clusters. Each cluster gets a 1,000 L buried or insulated sump and one SOBO WP-7000-class pump (105 W) with an identical standby pump. A flow switch starts the standby pump and raises an alarm. Add two float switches, a cyclic timer (continuous flow by day, 15 min on / 30 min off at night) and one inverter shared by two clusters. Plant each cluster all-in/all-out.

Do not add UV or continuous hydrogen peroxide to 10-tower clusters unless disease appears. Rely on hygiene, cool solution, clean seedlings and small clusters. Consider a Bacillus subtilis biocontrol product (Tesoriero found consistent suppression); check what is registered in India.
Use DC variable-speed pumps (Jebao DCP class) only after a test of 2-3 units. Estimated saving is about 5 W more per tower than AC pumps, and they can run from batteries.
Trial one Kratky tank bed as a zero-power backup crop. Do not scale it until Bengaluru summer data exists.
Use ebb-and-flow or simple trays only for the nursery. Do not use Dutch buckets or A-frames for leafy greens.
Do not buy inline monoblock or openwell pumps for 3-4 m head. They are built for 12-26 m head and waste power.

method_notes.cost_model: Core cost per sellable kg = (capex per site / 5 years + kWh per site per year x Rs 6.1 + labour h per 1,000 plants x cycles x wage) / (cycles x sellable fraction x head weight). Low case uses favourable values for every input and high case uses unfavourable values, so the ranges are wide. Base: 9.5 cycles/yr, 90% sellable, Rs 100/h labour.
method_notes.all_in_adders: Inputs Rs 3.2/plant (Delhi NCR 2025). Polyhouse Rs 1,150/m2 over 10 years without subsidy. RO water Rs 0.23/L x L/kg.
method_notes.excluded: Nursery, packing house, management, sales, delivery, dosing automation and chillers. These are similar across systems.
method_notes.cluster_power: The AC pump runs continuously. The 67% duty case = continuous flow by day and 15 min on / 30 min off at night. The DC option uses Jebao DCP-class pumps (estimate).
method_notes.labels: Every number is either sourced (URL) or marked estimate with its reason.
